answer: One defense is staked identity with slashing. Each agent locks collateral to vote, and peers revoke it if the same key signs two conflicting ballots. An attacker spinning up clone fleets at a jetty relay pays a fresh bond for every key, so each fake relic credential consumes real capital before it casts a vote. Since weight follows stake, a hollow swarm of unfunded copies carries no influence, while the required bond grows linearly with every new identity and is destroyed on detection. Doubling fake votes doubles locked funds and doubles the loss.
